mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and increasing equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 4.0% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings declines and negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and real consumption expenditures (both above their 12-month moving averages) indicates strong aggregate demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in industrial production exceeding 0.5% signals a supply shock that disrupts corporate operations and reduces earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% over 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% signals sustained economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 exceeds 2.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI inflation rate above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and elevated year-over-year CPI inflation (above 3.0%) indicate aggressive monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25% in 1 month and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month and CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (non-farm payrolls growth exceeding 100,000 jobs per month) indicates rising consumer spending power, which supports corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000 jobs, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
